questions.q: What does 'globally-distributed' mean for Cosmos DB, per this lesson?
options: Data is automatically replicated across Azure regions added to the account, as a built-in capability rather than a manual infrastructure project
Cosmos DB can only run in a single Azure region
It refers to Cosmos DB's marketing name, with no actual technical meaning
Global distribution requires the DBA to manually configure replica set members, just like self-hosted MongoDB
questions.explain: Adding a region is a configuration change; Cosmos DB automatically handles replication to it, unlike manually wiring up multi-region replica sets.

questions.q: What availability SLA does Cosmos DB guarantee for multi-region accounts?
options: 99.999% availability
100% availability with zero downtime guaranteed
95% availability
No availability SLA exists for Cosmos DB
questions.explain: Cosmos DB offers a financially-backed 99.999% ('five nines') availability SLA for accounts configured with more than one region.

questions.q: What latency guarantee does Cosmos DB provide for provisioned-throughput accounts?
options: Single-digit-millisecond latency (under 10ms) at the 99th percentile for reads and writes
Sub-second latency with no more specific guarantee
No latency guarantee is offered
100-millisecond latency at the 50th percentile only
questions.explain: Microsoft guarantees under 10ms at the 99th percentile — a specific, financially-backed commitment, not general marketing language.

questions.q: What does 'multi-model' mean for the Cosmos DB engine?
options: One underlying storage and distribution engine exposed through multiple API surfaces (Core, MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table)
Five completely separate databases bundled under one brand name
Cosmos DB requires using all five APIs simultaneously on every project
Multi-model refers only to Cosmos DB's pricing tiers
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: it's genuinely one engine with multiple API surfaces, not several separate databases.

questions.q: How does Cosmos DB's elastic scale differ from the MongoDB capacity planning framework in Lesson 28?
options: Throughput and storage scale automatically or via direct provisioning, without a DBA choosing a shard key or manually standing up new cluster members
Cosmos DB requires manually adding shard servers just like MongoDB
Cosmos DB has no scaling mechanism at all
Elastic scale means no partitioning design is ever needed
questions.explain: The lesson notes elastic scale handles scaling mechanics automatically, though partitioning design (Lesson 32) still requires real decisions.
